submitted.body:
A nonzero symmetric twenty-term element lies in the kernel of the degree-five second-kind interval transform. It therefore lies outside the predicted antisymmetric kernel. Exact rational elimination gives kernel dimension 13, compared with antisymmetric dimension 12. The operator uses the cited Ehrenborg–Readdy mixing rule; the paper explains the source misprint and the interpretation. Larger-degree computations and the remark concerning MathDB 347231 are distinguished from the principal certified counterexample.

**Result and scope:** Hetyei's kernel conjecture fails at n = 5 (dim ker I_2 = 13 > 12 = dim A_5) and, computationally, at n = 6, 7; it holds for n <= 4; 347231 (Conjecture 40) fails as a remark, without separate credit

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [A symmetric kernel certificate for Hetyei's second-kind interval transform: a refutation of the kernel conjecture (Discrete Comput. Geom. 2024, Conjecture 39)](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00059) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00059v1).

The paper page includes the supplementary proof-source JSON attachment and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the archived proof and verification sources. The linked paper gives the complete rigorous argument and specifies exactly which statements are formalized.
